releases.body:
Set up Claude Code, Codex 0.170+, OpenCode 1.x and Pi with one RedRouter API key.

Published as [@redrouter/cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@redrouter/cli):
```sh
export REDROUTER_API_KEY="your-key"
npx @redrouter/cli init
```

Requires Node.js 20.11+ and separately installed agents. Init merges settings, installs local OpenCode/Pi plugins, backs up changed files, and makes one test generation capped at 64 output tokens before saving. Keys stay in the environment. Use --dry-run to preview without generating.

Configuration behavior is unchanged from v0.1.0. This release adds scoped npm packaging and links to the [setup and troubleshooting guides](https://docs.redrouter.org/integrations). The GitHub-pinned installation remains available: npx github:redrouter/cli#v0.1.1 init.

Verified from the public registry in an isolated home and fresh npm cache: version, all four agent configurations, local plugins, live Messages probe, dry-run rerun and no saved API key. The registry tarball matches this release asset.

releases.name: RedRouter CLI v0.1.0
releases.body:
Set up Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode 1.x and Pi using one RedRouter API key and an explicit model.

Run:

export REDROUTER_API_KEY="your-key"
npx --yes github:redrouter/cli#v0.1.0 init

Requires Node.js 20.11+ and separately installed agent tools; Codex uses the current 0.170+ profile format. Init merges settings, installs local OpenCode/Pi provider plugins, backs up changed files, and makes one test generation capped at 64 output tokens. --dry-run previews paths; --skip-test configures without a generation. API keys stay in the environment.

Includes the MIT-licensed source and npm-ready tarball. The unscoped npm name redrouter belongs to another project; npm publication of @redrouter/cli is pending publisher authentication. GitHub installation is available now.

Validation: four installer behavioral tests, all three live API protocol probes, actual client configuration checks and plugin discovery. Claude Code, Codex and Pi completed real read-tool round trips. OpenCode returned a live response and registered the plugin; further read-tool checks encountered the restricted test key's spending cap and temporary-directory permissions. This does not override user permissions or raise key limits.
